WHAT COUNTS AS A RESEARCH ROLE?

Explicit titles. Visible boundaries.

  • Core UX ResearchUX Researcher, User Researcher, User Experience Researcher, UXR
  • Research OperationsResearch Ops and Research Operations titles
  • Adjacent researchDesign Researcher and Product Researcher

Title matching is a first pass. Generic “Researcher” and UX Designer titles are excluded; hybrid titles and missing variants need review.

Observed postings by year

Employers in this sample

Missing years mean no observed records, not zero market demand. Deduplication uses source + posting ID; cross-source reposts may remain. Changes in source coverage can create apparent growth.

BUILT ON EVIDENCE

Know the source. Know the limits.

01AVAILABLE NOW

Indeed Hiring Lab

Free historical national and sector indices. Monthly means calculated from daily seasonally adjusted total-posting indices. An index measures relative activity, not a count of open jobs.

Source & methodology ↗CC BY 4.0 · Aggregated by jobsAnalysis · Historical values may be revised.
02ACCESS REQUIRED

NLx Research Hub

A candidate for historical US posting records. Access requires an approved use case. Coverage and field availability must be assessed before comparing years.

Explore data access ↗No NLx records are currently included.
03LICENSE REQUIRED

Lightcast

A candidate for granular historical job-posting analysis. Confirm the available history, title filters, cost, and dashboard redistribution rights for the specific product.

Explore posting data ↗No Lightcast records are currently included.
Our unit of analysis is a posting, not a person hired.

We cannot infer hires, unemployment, or the impact of AI from posting counts alone. A credible UX Research trend needs a consistent source, stable title definition, deduplicated records, and explicit coverage by year. Salary and remote-work trends will follow once suitable fields and history are available.
